[[File:Sheaf of Planes.gif|frame|right|Sheaf of planes]]

In mathematics, a '''sheaf of planes''' is the set of all [[plane (geometry)|planes]] that have the same common [[line (geometry)|line]].<ref name="def">[https://mathworld.wolfram.com/SheafofPlanes.html Definition on ''Mathworld Wolfram'']</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Sommerville|first1=D. M. Y.|title=Classification of Geometries with Projective Metric|journal=Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society|date=1909|volume=28|pages=25–41|doi=10.1017/S0013091500034763|doi-access=free}}</ref> It may also be known as a '''fan of planes''' or a ''[[pencil of planes]]''.

When extending the concept of line to the ''[[line at infinity]]'', a set of ''[[parallel planes]]'' can be seen as a [[Sheaf (mathematics)|sheaf]] of planes intersecting in a line at infinity. To distinguish it from the more general definition, the adjective ''parallel'' can be added to it, resulting in the expression '''parallel sheaf of planes'''.<ref name="para">[https://www.vitutor.com/geometry/space/sheaf_planes.html Vitutor: Sheaf of Planes]</ref>
